name: GPT-Live-1
description: OpenAI's full-duplex voice model: it listens and speaks at the same time and hands deeper reasoning and tool use to a separate backend model. It powers ChatGPT Voice and has been in the API since September 2026.
strengths: Full duplex: handles pauses, interruptions and backchannels while it speaks
Delegates reasoning and tools to a backend model you choose, e.g. GPT-6 Astra
Flat $0.05 per minute, billed per second
21 built-in voices plus custom voices from a prompt or recording
weaknesses: Backend model and tool calls are billed separately on top of the per-minute rate
No image or video input on the API
Served only on the new Live endpoint (v1/live/sessions), not the Realtime API
notes: Notable: frontier-lab clause (also #3 on AA Speech to Speech Index at 83.2). releaseDate is the GPT-Live system card's publication date (2026-07-08), when GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1 mini became the ChatGPT Voice defaults; API general availability was 2026-09-10 per the OpenAI changelog. openai.com pages returned 403 to the fetcher, so launch-post facts come from the OpenAI developer community announcement, the changelog and the system card. AA's Big Bench Audio score (90.1%) is for 'GPT-Live-1 (Astra, medium)', i.e. paired with GPT-6 Astra at medium effort; with GPT-6 Sol (low) AA lists 89.0%. OpenAI's launch claims (paired with GPT-6 Astra medium): Tau3 83.6% vs 45.7% for GPT-Realtime-2.1, AA Conversational Dynamics 97.3%, turn-taking latency 0.798s. Voices: 12 at API launch, 9 more added 2026-10-16 (21 in the voice table). GPT-Live-1 mini (ChatGPT free-tier default) has no API listing and no separate entry. Languages: no total published; the voice table covers English, Portuguese, German, French, Hindi, Japanese and Korean.

pricing.notes: $0.05 per minute of live session, billed per second; backend Responses calls and tool use billed separately at the configured model's normal rates. No per-token audio pricing.

name: GPT-Live-1.1
description: An update to GPT-Live for ChatGPT, Codex and dots, with better accents, new voices and more natural delegation. API access is announced as coming soon.
strengths: 13 new voices
Better French, German, Hindi, Mexican Spanish, Korean and Japanese
Custom voices from a text prompt or an approved recording
weaknesses: Not in the API yet: OpenAI says only 'coming soon', and the API model list still shows gpt-live-1
No benchmark figures published for 1.1
notes: Notable: frontier-lab clause. Source is the OpenAI staff announcement on the OpenAI Developer Community (2026-10-15); the ChatGPT release notes (help.openai.com) returned 403. Third-party reports say a lighter 'GPT-Live-1.1 Quip' replaces GPT-Live-1 mini for non-Plus users, but the staff post doesn't mention Quip, so it isn't an entry and the claim is unverified. Not on the AA leaderboard. Consider whether a ChatGPT-only model belongs in the directory; the alternative is folding it into gpt-live-1's notes.

pricing.notes: No API pricing; available inside ChatGPT, Codex and dots.

name: GPT-Realtime-2.1
description: OpenAI's current Realtime API speech-to-speech reasoning model, with configurable reasoning effort and tool use. It updates GPT-Realtime-2 with better alphanumeric recognition, silence and noise handling, and interruption behavior.
strengths: Configurable reasoning effort in a single speech-to-speech model
Function calling and prompt caching on the Realtime API (WebRTC, WebSocket, SIP)
Accepts image input alongside audio and text
128K context, 32K max output
weaknesses: Audio at $32 in / $64 out per 1M tokens, far above per-minute rivals
Big Bench Audio drops from 95.8% at high effort to 86.8% at minimal (AA)
notes: Notable: frontier-lab clause (also #8 on AA Speech to Speech Index, 75.2 at High). AA Big Bench Audio: 95.8% (High), 86.8% (Minimal). OpenAI's deprecations page names gpt-realtime-2.1 as the replacement for gpt-realtime and gpt-4o-realtime (shutdown 2027-01-20). Knowledge cutoff 2024-09-30. Voices: 10 built-in Realtime voices (alloy, ash, ballad, coral, echo, sage, shimmer, verse, marin, cedar) per the Realtime conversations guide, and custom voices are available to eligible customers. No language count is published.

pricing.notes: Per 1M tokens: text $4 in / $0.40 cached / $24 out; audio $32 in / $0.40 cached / $64 out; image $5 in / $0.50 cached.

name: GPT-Realtime-2.1 Mini
description: A distilled, faster and cheaper version of GPT-Realtime-2.1 for realtime voice apps, with reasoning and tool use.
strengths: Audio at $10 in / $20 out per 1M tokens, under a third of GPT-Realtime-2.1
Function calling and reasoning tokens
OpenAI's named replacement for gpt-realtime-mini and its TTS models
weaknesses: Big Bench Audio 74.7% at High and 62.7% at Minimal (AA), far below the full model
notes: Notable: frontier-lab clause. AA lists 'GPT-Realtime-2.1 Mini High' at 74.7% and 'Mini Minimal' at 62.7% (S2S Index 54.4). OpenAI's deprecations page names it as the replacement for gpt-realtime-mini (shutdown 2027-01-20) and for tts-1, tts-1-hd and gpt-4o-mini-tts (shutdown 2027-01-06). 128K context, 32K max output. Voices: the same 10 Realtime voices.

pricing.notes: Per 1M tokens: text $0.60 in / $0.06 cached / $2.40 out; audio $10 in / $0.30 cached / $20 out; image $0.80 in / $0.08 cached.

name: GPT-Realtime-2
description: OpenAI's first Realtime API voice model with configurable reasoning, for speech-to-speech agents. It is still listed alongside its successor, GPT-Realtime-2.1.
strengths: Highest Big Bench Audio of any OpenAI model on AA, 96.6% at High
Configurable reasoning effort and function calling
128K context, 32K max output
weaknesses: Superseded by GPT-Realtime-2.1 at the same price
Big Bench Audio falls to 71.8% at minimal effort (AA)
notes: Notable: frontier-lab clause. Not deprecated on OpenAI's deprecations page, but GPT-Realtime-2.1 updates it at identical pricing; consider dropping it if the directory keeps only the newest generation. AA Big Bench Audio: High 96.6%, Medium 93.3%, Minimal 71.8%; S2S Index 73.6 (High).

pricing.notes: Per 1M tokens: text $4 in / $0.40 cached / $24 out; audio $32 in / $0.40 cached / $64 out; image $5 in / $0.50 cached.

name: GPT-Realtime-1.5

weaknesses: 32K context and 4,096 max output tokens

pricing.notes: Per 1M tokens: text $4 in / $0.40 cached / $16 out; audio $32 in / $0.40 cached / $64 out; image $5 in / $0.50 cached.

name: Gemini 3.8 Live
description: Google's default Live API model for low-latency voice agents, built on Gemini 3 Pro. It takes live audio, images and video and answers in speech, and it also powers Search Live.
strengths: Switches between 97 languages mid-conversation (Google launch post)
Asynchronous, non-blocking function calling plus Google Search grounding
Accepts live video and images as well as audio
Audio at $0.005/min in and $0.018/min out
weaknesses: Big Bench Audio 91.7%, behind its Extended Thinking sibling's 97.7% (AA)
Affective dialogue removed and proactive audio can't be switched off
notes: Notable: frontier-lab clause (also #9 on AA S2S Index, 74.5). GA 2026-09-15 per the Gemini API changelog. Google's launch post claims second place in AA's Speech Agent Arena. Language count conflicts: the launch post says 97, the Live API guide lists 99, and the Live API overview says 70. Voices: Google Cloud's Live API voice page lists 30 prebuilt voices for the Live API generally, not per model. 131,072 input / 65,536 output tokens. Knowledge cutoff January 2025 (model card).

pricing.notes: Paid tier, shared with 3.8 Live Extended Thinking and 3.1 Flash Live Preview: input text $0.75 / audio $3.00 (or $0.005/min) / image-video $1.00 (or $0.002/min) per 1M tokens; output text $4.50 / audio $12.00 (or $0.018/min) per 1M tokens, including thinking tokens. Free tier available. Google publishes separate per-minute input and output rates, not one blended per-minute price, so perMinuteUsd is null.

description: The higher-reasoning version of Gemini 3.8 Live, for complex multi-step voice tasks. It runs background reasoning at a configurable level while the conversation continues, and powers Gemini Live in the Gemini app.

Configurable background thinking: minimal, low, medium, high
Asynchronous function calling while audio keeps streaming
Same per-token price as Gemini 3.8 Live
weaknesses: 1.35s time to first audio on AA, among the slowest of the top models
τ-Voice 68.6%, behind GPT-Live-1 (74.5%) and Grok Voice 3.0 (71.6%) per xAI's comparison table

Google's launch post claimed #1 on AA's S2S index at 82.6; AA now ranks it 4th behind Phonic 1, Grok Voice 3.0 and GPT-Live-1. Google also reports τ-Voice-banking 35.1%. The AA listing is 'Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking (High)'. Language and voice counts as for Gemini 3.8 Live.

pricing.notes: Same table as Gemini 3.8 Live: input text $0.75 / audio $3.00 ($0.005/min) / image-video $1.00 ($0.002/min); output text $4.50 / audio $12.00 ($0.018/min) per 1M tokens, including thinking tokens.

name: Gemini 3.1 Flash Live

strengths: Big Bench Audio 96.6% at high thinking (AA)
Thinking levels from minimal to high
Same per-token price as Gemini 3.8 Live
weaknesses: Legacy preview: Google recommends migrating to Gemini 3.8 Live
Synchronous function calling only
2.99s time to first audio at high thinking (AA)

pricing.notes: Shares the Gemini 3.8 Live table: input text $0.75 / audio $3.00 ($0.005/min) / image-video $1.00 ($0.002/min); output text $4.50 / audio $12.00 ($0.018/min) per 1M tokens.

Flat $0.08 per minute, unchanged from Grok Voice 2.0
Built-in web search, X search, collections, MCP and custom function tools

Anyone on grok-voice-latest was switched on launch day unless they had pinned a version
Single region (us-east-1); sessions capped at 120 minutes

Launch figures (xAI citing AA): S2S Index 86.9 (2.0: 81.3), Big Bench Audio 98.5%, Speech Agent Arena Elo 1070, Task Success 94.8%, Full Duplex Bench 97.0%, τ-Voice 71.6% (GPT-Live-1 74.5%), ServiceNow EVA-Bench 74%. xAI's docs mark grok-voice-2.0 deprecated with no retirement date. Voices: the guide points to the TTS voice list, and the TTS docs list 5 built-in voices (ara, eve, leo, rex, sal) while an xAI cookbook mentions 28, so the count is left null. The launch post doesn't name tool calling, but the docs list it.

pricing.notes: $0.08/min ($4.80/hr) of session; text input messages $0.004 each; server_vad sessions billed for full session duration, push-to-talk only for audio sent and received.

18 voices, including polyglot voices that speak all 7 languages and code-switch
Same price as Nova 2 Sonic
256K context window
weaknesses: Only 7 supported languages; AWS advises against using others
No speech-to-speech translation, and pitch and accent can't be adjusted
Not yet on the AA leaderboard
notes: Not notable: Amazon isn't a frontier-lab company and the model isn't on AA. Languages: English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi. Regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-north-1, ap-northeast-1. Price not found: AWS says it matches Nova 2 Sonic, but the Bedrock pricing page's Nova speech rows didn't render for the fetcher.

name: Dessa
description: A full-duplex speech-to-speech model from Block's AI research lab, trained from scratch only on recorded human conversation, with no text and no pretrained models. It listens while it talks and runs locally on a high-end Mac.
strengths: Full duplex by design: backchannels and decides when to cut in
Trained only on human conversation audio, on a single NVIDIA GB200 NVL72
Runs locally on a MacBook Pro M4 Max or better
weaknesses: Waitlist only, with early access for a small group of AI safety researchers; no API or price
No benchmarks, latency figures or model size published
No text in training means no stated tool use; fact learning and new languages are listed as open questions
notes: Not notable: not on AA, and Block isn't a frontier-lab company. Moved from models.json; re-verified 2026-11-06 against block.xyz/dessa, which states the facts above but gives no publication date (only a privacy-notice effective date of 2026-10-21). releaseDate 2026-10-23 is carried over from the existing entry and news item (the announcement and Jack Dorsey's X post); it isn't printed on Block's page. The page lists no tool use, so toolCalling is null.

pricing.notes: No pricing published.

Calls tools while the caller is still speaking

pricing.notes: Starter $0.07/min (no minimum); Pro $0.065/min with $200/month minimum; Enterprise custom. $250/mo free credits for sign-ups by 2026-11-30.

pricing.notes: Audio input $0.0023/min, audio output $0.014/min, transcription input $0.0025/min; underlying token rates $0.75/1M input, $0.25/1M cached, $4.50/1M output. Separate in/out per-minute rates, so no single perMinuteUsd.

name: NemotronLabs VoiceChat 11B
description: NVIDIA's open-weight full-duplex speech model, an 11B hybrid Mamba/Transformer. NVIDIA calls it the first open full-duplex model that keeps the conversation going while it calls tools.
strengths: Open weights under OpenMDW 1.1
Tool calling with spoken 'on-hold' messages while tools run
448 ms turn-taking latency on Full-Duplex-Bench 1.0 (NVIDIA)
weaknesses: English only
Big Bench Audio 27.0% (AA)
No hosted API: self-serve via vLLM or an NGC NIM container
notes: Not notable: #41 on AA Big Bench Audio (27.0%, listed as 'Nemotron Voicechat'). Release date conflict: the model card says 2026-08-03, the NGC container page 2026-07-21. Licence conflict: the HF card says OpenMDW 1.1, but the NGC NIM container is under the NVIDIA Software and Model Evaluation License; the HF weights licence is used here. NVIDIA reports BFCL-v3 spoken tool calling 56.1%.

pricing.notes: Open weights; no hosted price.

name: PersonaPlex-7B
description: NVIDIA's open-weight 7B full-duplex speech-to-speech model, built on Kyutai's Moshi. A text prompt sets the persona and an audio prompt sets the voice.
strengths: Persona set by text prompt, voice by audio conditioning
Listens and speaks at once, with barge-in
Open weights, ready for commercial use per NVIDIA
weaknesses: English only
Big Bench Audio 19.1% (AA)
Gated Hugging Face download; self-host only
notes: Not notable: #42 on AA Big Bench Audio (19.1%). Release date per the model card (2026-01-15); secondary coverage says 2026-01-20. Licence: NVIDIA Open Model License Agreement, with additional information under CC-BY-4.0. The GitHub repo ships pre-packaged voice prompts (NATF0-3, NATM0-3, VARF0-4, VARM0-4), but the model card gives no count, so voices is null.

pricing.notes: Open weights; no hosted price.

name: Raon-SpeechChat 9B
description: KRAFTON's open-weight full-duplex speech language model for real-time English conversation, with natural turn-taking, backchannels and barge-in. It's built on the Raon-Speech base model.
strengths: Open checkpoints, training and inference pipeline
17 built-in personas plus voice cloning from reference audio
Strongest on Full-Duplex-Bench v1.0 turn-taking and interruption tasks (KRAFTON report)
weaknesses: Non-commercial licence (CC BY-NC 4.0)
English only
Big Bench Audio 57.5% (AA)
notes: Not notable: #37 on AA Big Bench Audio (57.5%). releaseDate is null: the HF card cites 'April 2026' with a technical report 'Published Apr 8', while the arXiv ID 2605.23912 implies May 2026. Training data: 119K hours (report) vs 116K hours (GitHub README). About 10B parameters despite the 9B name. No tool calling is mentioned, so toolCalling is null.

pricing.notes: Open weights; no hosted price.

name: Moshi
description: Kyutai's open-weight full-duplex spoken dialogue model, which models the user's and its own speech as parallel streams. It's the base that NVIDIA's PersonaPlex builds on.
strengths: About 200 ms practical latency on an L4 GPU (160 ms theoretical)
Weights CC-BY 4.0; runs on PyTorch, MLX and Rust/Candle
Inner-monologue text tokens alongside speech
weaknesses: Big Bench Audio 4.4%, last on AA
No tool access; English only
Two fixed synthetic voices (Moshiko, Moshika)
notes: Not notable: last on AA Big Bench Audio (#44, 4.4%). releaseDate is the open-weights release, from the Kyutai blog URL (/blog/2024-09-18-moshi-release); Kyutai first demoed Moshi in July 2024. Code licences: Python MIT, Rust Apache. 7B temporal transformer (the HF card lists 8B BF16 tensors). Older than the other entries but still available, so drop it if age matters. The HF card says the model is trained to produce one voice per checkpoint; the two released variants give 2 voices.

pricing.notes: Open weights; free online demo at moshi-chat.kyutai.org.

name: LFM3-Audio-2B
description: Liquid AI's small open-weight audio model. It takes speech or text and streams back text, speech or both, aimed at on-device voice chat.
strengths: Time to first token as low as 50 ms (causal encoder prefills while you speak)
About 2B parameters, in BF16, GGUF, MLX and ONNX
Turns spoken requests into tool calls
weaknesses: Voice chat is English only, though it understands 18 languages
Not on the AA leaderboard
No inference provider hosts it
notes: Not notable: not on AA. Included as a speech-in, speech-out streaming model, but the model card doesn't call it full duplex; drop it if the directory requires full-duplex realtime. languages = 18 (the header figure; the list has 19 entries because it separates British and American English). The licence record matches the LFM Open License v1.0 entry already in models.json.

pricing.notes: Open weights; Liquid AI API console linked but no price found.
